text.p: Cotton prices have dived in northern Nigeria only a month into the harvest season, the state-owned News Agency of Nigeria said on Tuesday.
Its investigation had shown a tonne of cotton was selling for 27,000 naira, against 40,000 three weeks ago.
Cotton firms in the area had owered their official purchasing price to 30,000 naira from 40,000.
The Cotton Merchants Association of Nigeria said the decline was due to low demand and the inability of the industry to exhaust old stocks.
"Licensed buyers who have direct links with the companies are not buying the commodity from us due to over-stocking of the produce," said farmer Haruna Isa.
Industry estimates put last year's Nigerian harvest at about 250,000 tonnes of seed cotton, which translates into roughly 90,000 tonnes of cotton lint after ginning.
Output is expected to be slightly higher or at least the same this year.
Senator Walid Jibrin, chairman of the Nigerian Textiles Manufacturers Association, said farmers were stuck with more than 400,000 bales of unsold cotton this season.
"Government should buy the excess cotton off the farmers, stock it and sell later to companies," he added.
